name: Aorto-ventricular tunnel

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and imaging criteria for aorto-ventricular tunnel diagnosis

criteria.description: Visualization of an abnormal tunnel-like communication between the ascending aorta and a ventricular chamber on echocardiography
Cardiac MRI demonstrating the extracardiac tunnel connecting the aorta to the ventricle
Presence of signs and symptoms of congestive heart failure or continuous cardiac murmur in infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of the tunnel via echocardiography or cardiac MRI with clinical correlation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily imaging-based; cardiac catheterization may be used for hemodynamic assessment.

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Normal inflammatory markers unless endocarditis present
imaging: Echocardiography showing tunnel between ascending aorta and ventricle
Cardiac MRI delineating extracardiac tunnel anatomy
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Hemodynamic assessment via cardiac catheterization may show left-to-right shunting

distinguishingFeatures: VSD involves defect in interventricular septum, not extracardiac tunnel
Echocardiography shows septal defect rather than tunnel
Communication between ascending aorta and pulmonary artery, not ventricle
Different surgical approach and imaging findings

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Continuous murmur with failure to thrive
Sudden onset of cyanosis or respiratory distress
references: Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2013.
Anderson RH, et al. Aorto-ventricular tunnel: anatomy and surgical considerations. Cardiol Young. 2010;20(3):253-259.
